name: Polka
classification_notes: Single-style display typeface built entirely around inflated, balloon-like letterforms. No weight axis, no italics, no condensed cut. Letterforms are fully rounded with a consistent puffed silhouette, placing this firmly in the decorative display category rather than any structural type classification.
summary: A puffed, balloon-style display face by Ian Adjeidu and Manas Trivedi, built for headline use in branding and editorial contexts where a soft, inflated aesthetic is the point.
description: Polka is a single-weight display typeface built around soft, inflated letterforms drawn from bubble and balloon typography. Designed by Ian Selorm Adjeidu and Manas Trivedi in 2022, it was conceived as a tool to let designers produce balloon-style type without lettering from scratch. Best suited to Illustrator and Photoshop, it fits experimental logos, magazine headlines and playful branding work.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by the wave of bubble and balloon type circulating on design-focused Instagram, Polka aims to give designers a whimsical, versatile typeface for making that aesthetic their own. The face works best in Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop, and is suited to logo design, branding and magazine use.

name: Pico
classification_notes: Single-weight decorative display face with deliberately uneven, high-contrast strokes built on a rule-of-thirds grid. The chaotic texture is held together by simple geometric shapes and a strict underlying structure. Inspired by Saul Bass mid-century title graphics and Stussy streetwear. No italic, condensed or mono variants.
summary: A single-weight display face of jagged, high-contrast strokes arranged on a rule-of-thirds grid, drawing on Saul Bass's mid-century title graphics and street graphics.
description: Pico is a decorative display typeface built from deliberately uneven, high-contrast lines arranged on a strict rule-of-thirds grid. It reads chaotic at first glance but holds together through its underlying geometric structure, pulling from Saul Bass's mid-century title work and Stussy's streetwear graphics. Suited to posters, clothing graphics, logos and editorial headlines where bold visual impact is the brief.
foundry_blurb: A display typeface inspired by the bold, graphic simplicity of Saul Bass and street graphics, Pico delivers high-contrast letterforms made from uneven lines on an underlying rule-of-thirds grid. Available as a commercial-use OTF for posters, clothing design, logos and magazines.

name: Glue
classification_notes: Single-weight hand-drawn display typeface with exaggerated rounded letterforms derived from balloon and bubble aesthetics. Ships in two styles – a solid filled variant and an outlined counterpart. No italics, no condensed cuts, no mono companion. Latin basic character set only.
summary: A hand-drawn bubble typeface in filled and outlined forms, built for punchy logo and headline work at display sizes.
description: Glue is a display typeface drawn from balloon and bubble letterforms, with exaggerated roundness and a hand-crafted weight. It ships in two complementary styles – a solid filled version and an outlined counterpart – giving designers room to layer or contrast them. The typeface suits large-scale work: logos, posters and editorial headers, and performs best in a vector environment such as Illustrator.
foundry_blurb: Hand-drawn typeface inspired by balloons and bubbles. A more elegant, refined take on bubble typography that works well for punchy, energetic logos and headers. Supplied as OTF and best used in a vector editing application such as Illustrator.

name: Gigo Type
classification_notes: Fluid calligraphic display face with a liquid, hand-drawn quality. Single OTF weight; no italics, condensed, or text variants. Note: the Gumroad page (manasseto.gumroad.com) belongs to Manas Trivedi, who collaborated with Ian Adjeidu on the POLKA typeface. Gigo Type appears to be Manas Trivedi's solo project attributed here under Ian Adjeidu per workflow specification. Designed for display-only use – chrometype effects and experimental logotypes. Not suited to running text.
summary: A fluid calligraphic display face drawn from the visual momentum of liquid, aimed at chrometype effects and experimental logotypes.
description: Gigo takes its form from the flowing quality of liquid, giving each letter a loose, hand-drawn momentum suited to large-scale display. Supplied as a single OTF, it is designed as a starting point rather than a finished system – the expectation is that designers will add their own shapes and modifications. Best used for chrometype treatments and experimental logos rather than set text.
foundry_blurb: A calligraphic typeface inspired by the momentum of liquid. Works well for chrometype designs and experimental logos, and can serve as a customisable base for further lettering explorations.

name: Juicy
classification_notes: Condensed sans-serif structure with exaggerated bubbly rounded letterforms. Thick, blocky, bold display face with soft edges and pronounced stroke width. Single-weight OTF. The condensed skeleton gives it solidity while the rounding keeps it playful.
summary: A chunky, bubbly display face built on a condensed sans-serif skeleton, with soft rounded edges and thick bold letterforms designed for cheerful commercial work.
description: Juicy is a round, bubbly display typeface built on a condensed sans-serif structure, giving it a thick, blocky character. The curvaceous letterforms balance a playful aesthetic with legibility, making it suited to branding, poster work and logo design. Sold as a single OTF file, licensed for personal and commercial use.
foundry_blurb: A playful, round bubbly display typeface with curvaceous soft edges and thick bold letterforms. Juicy blends bubbly lettering with legibility and uniformity, making it a solid pick for projects that need a touch of fun.
